application_review: PROGRESS. The preceding eligibility-check turn reconfirmed the official complete-proof submission route. The previous proof round was rechecked before edits; retained proof hashes are unchanged.
The hull is the actual finite convex hull of mixed dual functions with unit-bounded nonroot inputs. It is not an arbitrary space postulated to have the desired properties.
Products of generators enter the hull by the previously proved exact averaged dual expansion. Two uses of convex-hull minimality extend this to arbitrary hull members.
The hull contains one, is closed under finite products and all ambient translations, and remains pointwise unit-bounded. These statements also cover degree zero.

The anti-uniform correlation bound requires positive degree and permits arbitrary real-valued test functions. The weighted form requires nonnegative weights summing to one and keeps those same weights.

One definition and ten theorems are audited. Finite convex closure does not establish topological or Loeb closure, characteristic-factor localization, different-subgroup concatenation, or the full higher-order Bessel theorem.
